artifacts.summary: Finds, via gh run view --log on all 3 failing runs, that docgen-action's own internal 'Cache Mathlib docs' actions/cache step has never saved (post-if: success() gate; the job always fails), forcing every run to cold-build the full ~6,300-target Mathlib+dependency docInfo fan-out instead of restoring it -- the dominant driver of the process-spawn ENOMEM, and a self-reinforcing loop independent of LEAN_NUM_THREADS or swap size. Recommends an additive if: always() actions/cache/save step in docs.yml (no fork needed, same key/path docgen-action already computes) as the primary fix; explicit removal of the refuted-and-harmful LEAN_NUM_THREADS env var; a version-verified linglib-precedent doc-gen4-CLI-bypass (find | xargs -P N calling doc-gen4 single/fromDb directly) as a documented fallback if the cache fix alone is insufficient; and vm.overcommit_memory sysctl tuning plus /proc/meminfo instrumentation as a cheap secondary layer. Flags that verification needs two pushed runs (first repopulates the cache, second proves the fan-out shrank), not one.

memory_candidates.content: A GitHub Actions composite/third-party action's own internal actions/cache step can be permanently defeated when its save (post) action is gated post-if: success() and the job it's embedded in always fails before reaching success -- confirmed for leanprover-community/docgen-action's 'Cache Mathlib docs' step (actions/cache@v4.2.3, post-if: success()) across 3 consecutive failing BimodalLogic docs.yml runs, all showing 'Cache not found for input keys: ...' plus outcome=skipped on the save post-action. Diagnosis: gh run view <id> --log, grep for 'Cache not found'/'outcome=skipped'. Fix: add an independent, if: always()-gated actions/cache/save step replicating the SAME cache key (hashFiles formula) and path list the wrapped action's own index.js computes, placed after the failing step -- this persists whatever partial work (e.g. markers for thousands of successfully-built sub-targets before a late OOM) exists on disk at job end even though the overall job status is failure, breaking an otherwise-permanent cold-cache loop.

doc-gen4's Lake library_facet `docs` (and module_facet `docInfo`) recursively fetches docInfo for every transitive IMPORT of a library's root modules, not just the library's own modules -- so `lake build <lib>:docs` on a Mathlib-dependent project spawns one external doc-gen4 process per module in the ENTIRE transitive import closure (Mathlib itself included), not per-module-of-the-target-library. Confirmed by reading doc-gen4's own lakefile.lean at the exact pinned tag matching the consuming project's lean-toolchain. This is also independently corroborated by a different real project's (linglib) production docs.yml history, which hit the identical OOM and fixed it by bypassing the :docs facet entirely in favor of calling the doc-gen4 CLI's own `single`/`fromDb` subcommands directly, scoped only to its own modules, with explicit xargs -P N concurrency instead of relying on Lake's job scheduler or LEAN_NUM_THREADS.

Lake 5.0.0's CLI accepts no job-count flag in ANY position: neither `lake build -j2`/`lake build --jobs=2` (as a build-subcommand flag) nor `lake -j 2 build ...`/`lake -j2 --version` (as a global pre-subcommand flag) -- all four forms return 'unknown short/long option'. A since-abandoned commit in a different Lean project (linglib) had used the global-flag form historically, but that project itself later abandoned the Lake-facet + -j approach entirely (switching to direct doc-gen4 CLI invocation) because even a working -j flag would not have been sufficient -- the facet-level fan-out into Mathlib's import closure was the actual problem, not Lake's own concurrency level.
